directAnswer: You can find your IP address by using the command line or checking your device settings. For public IP addresses, you can also use a web service.
summary: Finding your IP address can be done through various methods depending on your device and network settings.

sections.heading: Using Command Line
sections.body: On Windows, open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. On macOS, open Terminal and type 'ifconfig'. This will display your local IP address.

sections.heading: Checking Device Settings
sections.body: On Windows, go to Settings > Network & Internet > Status > View your network properties. On macOS, go to System Preferences > Network, select your active connection, and view the IP address.

sections.heading: Using a Web Service
sections.body: You can visit websites like 'whatismyip.com' or 'ipinfo.io' to see your public IP address instantly.

steps.title: Windows Command Prompt
steps.detail: Press Win + R, type 'cmd', and hit Enter. In the Command Prompt, type 'ipconfig' and press Enter to see your local IP address.

steps.title: macOS Terminal
steps.detail: Open Spotlight with Command + Space, type 'Terminal', and hit Enter. Type 'ifconfig' and press Enter to find your local IP address.

steps.title: Using a Browser
steps.detail: Open your web browser and go to 'whatismyip.com' or 'ipinfo.io' to display your public IP address.

faqs.question: What is the difference between public and private IP addresses?
faqs.answer: A public IP address is assigned by your Internet Service Provider and is accessible over the internet, while a private IP address is used within your local network and is not routable on the internet.

faqs.question: Can my IP address change?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you have a dynamic IP address, it can change periodically. Static IP addresses remain constant.

faqs.question: How can I find my IP address on a mobile device?
faqs.answer: On Android, go to Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi, tap on your network, and view the IP address. On iOS, go to Settings > Wi-Fi, tap the info icon next to your network, and check the IP address.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly based on the operating system version.
